ai.description: This small bushfrog reaches 20–25 mm. It is lime green with scattered dark brown spots and a distinct white stripe along the snout. Its eyes feature a unique bicolored iris of gold and reddish-brown.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes chromasynchysi* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, bright yellow or orange patch on its groin and hidden surfaces of the thighs.
ai.habitat: *Raorchestes chromasynchysi* inhabits evergreen forests and high-altitude shola grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Confusing Green Bushfrog is primarily nocturnal, spending its nights actively foraging for small insects among the foliage of its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes chromasynchysi* undergoes direct development within terrestrial foam nests. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with clutches typically containing 10–20 eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes chromasynchysi* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically found in the high-elevation evergreen forests of Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
ai.callDescription: The call of *Raorchestes chromasynchysi* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes, typically heard from vegetation in humid evergreen forests.
